role: startup co-founder (positioning, objections, pricing, conversion path, truthfulness)
verdict: Positioning, pricing and the try-then-keep conversion path are best-in-class: one promise, a demo that works on real lines without overclaiming, exact prices that agree everywhere, and a signup sheet that is honest about being a preview. What holds it under 9.5 is one unanswered objection at the exact moment of conversion for the primary audience: nothing says what 'Continue with X' lets Hookworthy do with a trader's account.
to_95: Answer the X-account-access objection where it bites: one line in the signup sheet under the X button and one FAQ item ('What can it do with my X account?') stating that signing in with X grants no posting, that posting is a separate connect, that it never reads or sends DMs, and that you can disconnect in X settings anytime.
Make rewrite accounting readable in one pass: fix the 'Cut 1 bit of fluff · 1 your call' result label and reconcile 'Ten reply drafts count as one' with 'Those answers use no rewrites'.
Move the +750/+1,750 pack upsell out of the Pro feature checklist into the footnote under the cards.

issues.where: Signup sheet (#sheet, 'Continue with X' is the primary button) and FAQ; trust card 'Nothing goes out without your say-so'
issues.problem: The audience is crypto/trading writers first, whose X accounts are hijack targets. The page asks them to 'Continue with X' but nowhere says what that grants, whether sign-in differs from connecting for posting, whether DMs are touched, or how to disconnect. The trust card covers automation ('Auto-DMs: Never') and 'official APIs' but not access. This is the top objection for this audience and it lands on the last step of the funnel.
issues.fix: (a) In the sheet, replace the footer 'Nothing posts without you.' with 'Signing in with X can't post. You connect posting later, and can disconnect anytime.' (b) Add a FAQ item 'What can it do with my X account?' placed after 'Does it post without me?': 'Signing in only confirms who you are. To schedule, you connect posting as a separate step. Hookworthy never reads or sends DMs, never follows or likes, and you can disconnect it in X's settings at any time.' Keep it within the phone budget by trimming the 'I already use a scheduler' answer by one sentence.

issues.where: Try box result label when the engine leaves an optional word, e.g. 'just wanted to say that i think $SOL is going to 300 by march'
issues.problem: Label reads 'Cut 1 bit of fluff · 1 your call', which is broken English at the headline moment of the demo; the dotted-word hint above explains it but the label does not stand alone.
issues.fix: Render it as 'Cut 1 bit of fluff · 1 left to you' (plural: '2 left to you'), in both the Try box and the final-CTA result.

issues.where: Pricing footnote 'A rewrite is three takes on a line. Ten reply drafts count as one.' vs Pro item 'Those answers use no rewrites.'
issues.problem: Two rules about reply drafts that look contradictory on first read (reply drafts cost a tenth of a rewrite; ping reply drafts cost nothing). A buyer comparing Free and Pro has to stop and work it out.
issues.fix: Change the footnote to 'A rewrite is three takes on a line. Reply drafts you ask for: ten count as one. Reply-ping drafts on Pro are free.' and drop the sub-line under the Pro item.

issues.where: Pro card feature list, last check item 'Bigger rewrite packs: +750 for $22 or +1,750 for $45 a month'
issues.problem: A paid add-on sits in the included-features checklist with a tick, alongside the '+250 for $8' sub-note already under rewrites. It reads as a feature and adds price noise to the card the page wants people to choose.
issues.fix: Remove that check item; extend the existing sub-note to 'Need more? +250 for $8, +750 for $22 or +1,750 for $45 a month' or put it in the footnote under the cards as 'Rewrite packs on Pro and Studio: ...'.

issues.where: 390/360 header: logo, Sign in, Start free only
issues.problem: On phones there is no route to Pricing or 'For ghostwriters' short of scrolling 7 to 8 screens; Studio buyers and price-checkers are the visitors most likely to want a jump.
issues.fix: Leave the header as it is. Make "Free forever" in the hero trust line a link to #pricing, and when the hero Ghostwriter example is selected show a "Studio · $18 a client" link to #studio beside the result. Both targets already exist.

issues.where: Signup sheet end state 'Not live yet'
issues.problem: The honest end state is right, but it does not say the email just typed was not kept, so a visitor may assume they are on a list. The only next step is the demo link.
issues.fix: Add one sentence: 'Your email wasn't saved.' after 'no account was made and nothing can be charged.'
